comparisons.peer_summary: The firm's share repurchase program aims to maintain appropriate common equity levels and is effected through open-market purchases and accelerated share repurchases, with amounts and timing determined by capital position, deployment opportunities, regulatory requirements, market conditions, and stock price.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Goldman Sachs disclosed share repurchase programs in their 2024 filings, but the nature of the disclosure differs. JPMorgan specifically reported a new $30 billion Board authorization effective July 1, 2024. In contrast, Goldman Sachs described the general policy of its program intended to maintain common equity levels, utilizing open-market purchases and accelerated share repurchases, without explicitly detailing a new specific dollar authorization amount in the same manner as JPMorgan's announcement.

sentences.text: On June 28, 2024, the Firm announced that its Board of Directors had authorized a new $30 billion common share repurchase program, effective July 1, 2024.
The firm's share repurchase program is intended to help maintain the appropriate level of common equity.

The share repurchase program is effected primarily through regular open-market purchases (which may include repurchase plans designed to comply with Rule 10b5-1 and accelerated share repurchases), the amounts and timing of which are determined primarily by the firm's current and projected capital position, and capital deployment opportunities, but which may also be influenced by the evolution of current and future regulatory capital requirements, general market conditions and the prevailing price and trading volumes of the firm's common stock.

comparisons.peer_summary: On June 28, 2024, the Board authorized a multi-year $20 billion common stock repurchase program starting in Q3 2024 without an expiration date, with the Firm considering segment capital needs and benefit plan obligations in its execution.
comparisons.comparison: Both JPMorgan and Morgan Stanley disclosed new share repurchase authorizations on June 28, 2024, representing a synchronous event among peers. However, the programs differ in scale and structure: JPMorgan authorized a $30 billion program effective July 1, 2024, which replaced a prior $30 billion program, whereas Morgan Stanley authorized a $20 billion multi-year program starting in Q3 2024 with no expiration date.

sentences.text: On June 28, 2024, the Firm announced that its Board of Directors had authorized a new $30 billion common share repurchase program, effective July 1, 2024.
Through June 30, 2024, the Firm was authorized to purchase up to $30 billion of common shares under its previously-approved common share repurchase program that was announced on April 13, 2022.

On June 28, 2024, the Firm announced that its Board of Directors reauthorized a multi-year repurchase program of up to $20 billion of outstanding common stock (the "Share Repurchase Authorization"), without a set expiration date, beginning in the third quarter of 2024, which will be exercised from time to time as conditions warrant.
